chapter: Technique, jam sessions, audiences and records
title: Where jam sessions happened; Peck Kelly
summary: Jamming was in Kansas City good-time houses, since dance halls shut up; Smith never heard Peck Kelly in person.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you ever hear that White piano player he's always going on about -- Peck Kelly?
Peck Kelly? No. I never did get to hear him in person. I heard some of his records and I heard him on the radio, but I never did get to hear him in person.
He's supposed to be good, isn't he?

Yeah. He never would come by to jam with us. In fact, most of the jamming places were in Kansas City. They didn't have none in Oklahoma City; it was just right in (?) houses or something like that. But the dance hall... They didn't have no nightclubs around there. The (?) didn't have none. I remember all of them dance halls, after the dance they'd close up and they wouldn't let you up there.
Would you stay in the dance hall to jam after it was closed up?
No, no. The guy locked things up, and ran everybody out.
So you just went to people's apartments.
Mmm-hmm, yeah. We knew where the people had a good-time house, serving meals around there and serving drinks, (?) stuff, and they'd go out and dance all night. Pretty good size.
